chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say:

There is no harm in allowing women to be sent ahead when the night has passed. They should stand at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām for a short while, then be taken to Minā, where they stone the Jamrah. Then they should wait a short while, then shorten their hair, and be taken to Makkah to perform tawaf, unless they want a sacrifice to be slaughtered on their behalf, in which case they appoint someone to slaughter on their behalf.

key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, where pilgrims perform parts of the hajj rites including stoning
key_terms.يَطُفْنَ: they perform tawaf around the Kaʿbah
key_terms.يُقَصِّرْنَ: they shorten their hair as part of the ritual completion
key_terms.يُوَكِّلْنَ: they appoint an agent to perform the sacrifice on their behalf
key_terms.ٱلنِّسَاءُ: women pilgrims referred to in this ruling
key_terms.ٱلْجَمْرَةَ: the Jamrah that is stoned during the hajj rites
key_terms.ٱلْمَشْعَرِ ٱلْحَرَامِ: al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, the sacred site at Muzdalifah where pilgrims stop

ai.seo_question: Can women leave Muzdalifah before Fajr and complete their hajj rites early?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning women during the rites of hajj, permitting them to depart early from Muzdalifah after the night has passed. It outlines the sequence of their rites in Mina and Makkah and allows them to appoint someone to perform the sacrifice on their behalf.
